# Pandamonium v1.0.38

Arrange projects and chats across configured agents, keep independent worker layouts, and use rounded workspace controls that follow your Pandamonium theme.

## MAD-873 — Workspace UI: unify agent sidebar controls and theme-aware selectors

### Problem

Ordinary chat reorder handles were hidden behind rearrange mode, while catalog worker pins and ordering were restricted to the local Codex path. Saving one agent's visible project order could discard another agent's order. The selector and Details styling did not consistently follow theme colors, and runtime labels incorrectly described remote Codex connections as workstation connections.

### Implementation

Shared sidebar handles are visible by default. Catalog workers use the existing drag, keyboard, preference, and five-row expansion behavior. Layouts are saved per worker; pins include both project and task identity. Ordinary project reorder preserves other agents' saved projects. Explicit handles inside catalog buttons now support touch dragging.

The conversation picker, model control, effort track, and Details card use rounded shapes and theme tokens. The native model dropdown gains a rounded popup where the browser supports customizable selects, with a native fallback. Selector and Details labels distinguish assigned identity, verified runtime capability, and configured execution location.

### Product value and UI visibility

Reorder projects and chats from their visible handles or with Alt + Up/Down, pin catalog tasks, and reveal five additional chats per Show more click. Switching agents and reloading preserves saved layouts. Model and effort controls and the Details card change colors with the selected theme. User-assigned identity names remain installation data rather than fixed product names.

### Verification

Browser checks cover ordinary-agent order preservation, worker isolation, duplicate task references across projects, pin order and reload, touch dragging, native model/effort selection, dark/light theme changes, and phone layout. Backend checks validate runtime/location projection and existing bounded discovery behavior. Full regression and release validation results are recorded in the linked implementation PR.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No new dependency, database schema, bridge installation, or data migration is required. Existing local Codex desktop seeds and owner preferences are retained. Catalog layouts are scoped to the configured worker target and do not write back to the external agent. Reordering does not move projects, change working directories, or alter execution permissions.

Tailnet discovery currently finds supported model endpoints on selected nodes. Codex/Claude installation capabilities are reported through configured bridges; this release does not add detection of arbitrary bare CLI installations. Runtime/location text reflects configured metadata, not a new filesystem inspection. Reasoning and work-budget behavior is unchanged. The existing MCP response/recovery issue remains open. Install the published release through the normal updater.
